design.site_summary: A partial shade balcony with dry soil conditions and no pets in the household.
design.layout_strategy: The planting is structured vertically with trailing succulents on the edge railing, upright structural shrubs and herbs at mid-height against the back wall, and low rosette succulents creating a dense ground-level edge.
design.combination_logic: The scheme combines architectural uprights with soft cascading textures and tight rosettes, offering a contrast of grey-green foliage, aromatic textures, and smooth succulent surfaces that maintain their appearance year-round with minimal seasonal change.

zones.placement: on the outer partial shade railing, receiving filtered morning light and good air circulation

plants.why: Adapts well to low moisture and partial shade while producing neat rosettes.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides a neat, sculptural edge detail and soft blue-green colour contrast against the metallic railing.

maintenance: Water sparingly only when the soil is completely dry
Remove any dead lower leaves annually in spring
Repot every two years into fresh gritty succulent compost

zones.placement: against the rear balcony wall in partial shade, sheltered from strong winds

plants.why: Thrives in dry partial shade and provides height and a strong lemon fragrance.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as the vertical backdrop and focal height anchor, contrasting with the stiff foliage of the succulents.

plants.why: Handles dry conditions and low moisture with ease in partial shade.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds velvety grey-green texture and mid-height mass that bridges the gap between tall shrubs and low succulents.

maintenance: Water every 10 days during summer, monthly in winter
Prune back woody stems by one-third in early spring to encourage bushy new growth
Feed with a balanced slow-release fertiliser once in mid-spring

zones.placement: in wide shallow containers along the balcony floor edge in partial shade

plants.why: Tolerates low moisture and partial shade effortlessly.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides striking vertical sword-like leaf accents at the base that contrast with the rounded rosettes and bushy herbs.

plants.why: A drought-tolerant succulent suited to low moisture environments.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds woody stems and fleshy green leaves, creating a miniature tree-like structure at the lower layer.

maintenance: Water thoroughly only when soil is completely dry
Wipe dust from the leaves with a damp cloth as needed
Repot every 3 to 4 years when root-bound

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture levels across all containers with a finger test before watering
care_instructions.frequency: every 10 to 14 days in summer, every 4 weeks in winter

care_instructions.task: Prune back the Lemon Verbena and Sage to maintain compact form and encourage fresh shoots
Clear away any fallen debris from the surface of the pots to prevent fungal issues

care_cautions: Overwatering the Echeveria elegans and Crassula argentea in the cooler months can cause stem rot and leaf drop.
The Aloysia triphylla may suffer from frost damage if left exposed during freezing winter conditions and should be moved to a protected spot.
design.pet_safety_note: There are no pets in the household, ensuring that aromatic and succulent species can be grown safely without risk of ingestion.
